solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Club redeployed subtle means to move campaigners

parts.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball

indicators.note: redeployed means these letters are put back into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A golf club or nightclub cleverly reorganised so that political canvassers can be shuttled about.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle bus is the coach a party's election team tours the country in during a campaign.

clue.text: Heading for bar, make eyes at spirit

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of bar is used

parts.note: to make eyes at someone is to ogle them

explanation.surface: Someone at a pub counter flirting with a ghost, or with a glass of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogle is a goblin or phantom in Scottish and northern English folklore, a kind of supernatural being.

clue.text: Right policy with which revolutionary is splitting room

parts.note: which and that are interchangeable relative pronouns
Che Guevara is the stock crossword revolutionary

indicators.note: splitting means the word is goes into the middle of the abbreviation for room, cutting it in two

explanation.surface: A right-wing programme in which a rebel is dividing the chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctrines of Margaret Thatcher are the classic British example of a right-wing political programme.

clue.text: Mathematician to overtake doctor

parts.note: to lap a rival in a race is to overtake them a full circuit ahead
to doctor a drink is to lace it with something

explanation.surface: A mathematician racing past a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Simon Laplace was a celebrated French mathematician and astronomer, the Laplace transform being named after him.

clue.text: Rockers, perhaps old, getting plastered?

parts.note: a group of rock musicians is an example of a band
old means aged

explanation.surface: Ageing rock musicians getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' looks like slang for drunk, which suits the rockers, but it means covered in sticking plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound covered in plasters or dressings has been bound up with surgical material.

clue.text: Top marks repeated in match

indicators.note: in means the doubled letter sits inside the word for match

parts.note: to suit is to match or go well with

indicators.note: repeated means the single letter for marks is written down twice

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for the mark, the former German currency

explanation.surface: Top marks earned over and over during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is the highest point of a mountain, its peak.

clue.text: Split blades

definitions.meaning: to inform on someone to the police, British slang
the narrow leaves that make up a lawn

explanation.surface: Something cut apart by sharp edges.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to grass is to squeal or inform, and grass is also what lawn leaves are made of.

clue.text: Bottom of bag has more spare, one gathers

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom of a word is its final letter

parts.note: spare in the sense of thin or lean, so more spare is leaner

explanation.surface: The base of a sack holds a thinner figure, and somebody collects it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleaner collects leftover grain after the harvest, or more generally gathers scraps of information.

clue.text: A journey back

parts.note: to go is to travel or journey

explanation.surface: A return trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a reversal signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Back in the sense of in the past, as in 'years back', means the same as years before now.

clue.text: Unlicensed bar, getting tip to stop the drink, suddenly emptied

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so the word for tip goes into the middle of the drink

parts.note: the drink is slang for the sea
a peak is a tip or summit

indicators.note: emptied means the inner letters are removed, leaving only the outside two

explanation.surface: An illegal drinking den where someone is told to quit drinking and the glass is suddenly drained.
explanation.definitionFit: A speakeasy was a secret bar selling alcohol illegally, especially during US Prohibition.

clue.text: Understand a minimum of government file

indicators.note: the smallest possible part of the word, a single opening letter

parts.note: a rasp is a coarse file for shaping wood

explanation.surface: Getting your head round a bit of a civil-service dossier.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to comprehend it fully.

clue.text: Hit head

definitions.meaning: a record at the top of the charts
the boss, the person in charge

explanation.surface: A blow to the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart-topping single is a number one, and the top person in an organisation is also its number one.

clue.text: Having stolen kiss, on camera, ma fiddling with kilt!

definitions.text: Having stolen kiss, on camera, ma fiddling with kilt!

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take in another letter, as if pocketing it
fiddling with means messing about with these letters to rearrange them

parts.note: X is the conventional symbol for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A mother caught on film snatching a kiss while tugging at a kilt: shocking!
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the wordplay, and as a whole its outrage ends in the very symbol it describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The scene described is startling enough to deserve the punctuation sign written after an exclamation, which the clue itself ends with.

clue.text: A m-monkey, say, with caged beast getting loose

indicators.note: caged means the animal is enclosed within the stuttered word

parts.note: a monkey is an example of a primate, and the stammered m-monkey asks for its first letter to be stuttered too
an ox is a beast of burden

explanation.surface: A stammering zookeeper reports a monkey and a caged animal escaping.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'm-monkey' signals a stammer, so the synonym for monkey is written with its opening letter doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose estimate or translation is a rough, inexact one.

clue.text: Run through gardens before accessing sacred hollow

indicators.note: the gardens and the word for before enter into the shell of sacred
a hollow word has had its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Someone races across a park before entering a holy cave.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone through is to pierce them with a blade, as a kebab is pierced.

clue.text: One teaching a pig, possibly, to catch large snail

indicators.note: the made-up trainer's title takes in the letter for large

parts.note: a female pig is a sow, so a trainer of one might be a sow coach
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A farmyard trainer tries to teach a pig to grab a big mollusc.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail is a figurative slowpoke, someone who dawdles and lags behind.

clue.text: Strong liquor: relative's also knocked out by a pint, initially?

indicators.note: one word is ousted from the relative and replaced with the opening letters

parts.note: a grandpa is a relative, the possessive simply linking to what follows
and means also, as in 'this and that'

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: An old relative floored by a single pint of strong spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is a potent Italian brandy distilled from grape pomace.

clue.text: Shape is round about a square

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about, or around, the a
to shape something is to mould it into a new form, so these letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle: a circle drawn around a square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like part of the geometry, but it is the definition: an old-fashioned person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a fuddy-duddy, someone hopelessly behind the times and out of touch.

clue.text: In a state, I'm surprised current nation has squandered millions

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise
I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: to squander something is to lose it, so the letter goes from the nation

parts.note: Oman is a nation in the Arabian peninsula
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Someone flustered by a country that has wasted vast sums.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ohioan is a resident of the US state of Ohio, someone living in a state.

clue.text: A vessel containing mostly lush fruit

indicators.note: the vessel holds the shortened word inside it

parts.note: a pot is a cooking or storage vessel

indicators.note: mostly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: lush means rich, as in rich or luxuriant growth

explanation.surface: A container brimming with something luxurious and fruity.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit related to the plum.

clue.text: After U-turn, a top politician procrastinating

indicators.note: a U-turn means going back the way you came, so these words are read backwards

parts.note: a lid is a top for a container
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A senior politician dithering after a policy reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilatory means slow to act, given to delay and putting things off.

clue.text: Weapon transported to the north in carriages safely

indicators.note: in a down entry, carrying letters northwards means they read from bottom to top
in says the letters lie inside these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Arms smuggled north in railway carriages without incident.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Weapon transported' as the definition, but 'transported' belongs to the reversal signal: the letters are carried upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used by southern African peoples such as the Zulu.

clue.text: In the Bible he hunted game with stick

parts.note: nim is a mathematical game of removing counters
a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: A biblical hunter armed with a stick goes after game.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis calls Nimrod a mighty hunter before the Lord, and his name has come to mean any keen huntsman.

clue.text: Fractured no more, I care to protect bone, whatever happens

indicators.note: the scrambled letters surround the bone, shielding it
fractured means broken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the shin is the shinbone, or tibia

explanation.surface: An injured person declaring they no longer mind guarding a broken bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in any circumstances at all, regardless of the weather or anything else.

clue.text: Character reference fraudulent, with no truthfulness, all concluding

indicators.note: the concluding letter of each of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A dishonest character reference, utterly lacking in truth.
explanation.definitionFit: The ethos of a person or community is its distinctive spirit, moral nature or guiding beliefs.

clue.text: Evergreen song by artist breaking Chaucer's heart

indicators.note: the artist breaks into those central letters
the heart of a word is its central letters

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a recognised artist
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A tune written by a painter cracking the core of a medieval poet's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Araucaria is the genus of conifers including the monkey puzzle tree, which keeps its leaves all year.

clue.text: Trouble when leader vacates post

indicators.note: the leading letter leaves the word, so it is dropped

parts.note: post and mail both mean letters and parcels delivered

explanation.surface: Problems arise when the boss quits the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to trouble or afflict, as in 'what ails you?'

clue.text: One's plotted revenge, primarily, in break with French at last

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the break

parts.note: a gap is a break or interval

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter is taken
at last means the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone plotting revenge during a holiday with the French, finally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plotted' suggests scheming revenge, but it refers to points drawn on a chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A graph is a diagram on which data points are plotted against axes.

clue.text: Meeting fate, male serf

indicators.note: meeting means the male comes up against fate, so one is placed right before the other

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: A man meeting his destiny as a bonded labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Helots were the state-owned bondsmen of ancient Sparta, so the word means any serf.

clue.text: Being obscene about right, comic insisted

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about the abbreviation for right
comic means farcical or absurd, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A comedian insisted on being smutty about the right wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirtiness here means smuttiness or indecency, the quality of being lewd.
